symptom: The standalone untrusted source-manifest reference digest accepted an identifier containing an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate. Node.js replaces that code unit with U+FFFD during UTF-8 encoding, so distinct caller-owned manifest identifiers could produce the same content reference digest without a SHA-256 collision. A local Node 22.16.0 synthetic probe reproduced high-surrogate, low-surrogate and literal replacement-character aliases; no private or production evidence was used.
lesson: Length-prefixing and SHA-256 do not distinguish malformed JavaScript strings when UTF-8 conversion replaces unpaired UTF-16 with U+FFFD. The standalone source-manifest reference identifier must be well-formed before computing its untrusted correlation digest; this is distinct from the standalone proof-request transcript boundary.
guardrail: Reject isolated high/low UTF-16 surrogates in source-manifest manifestId before contentHash. Keep the standalone digest return contract null for invalid identifiers; retain valid surrogate pairs and the unchanged valid reference digest. Exercise high-surrogate and low-surrogate versus U+FFFD aliases with a synthetic regression. Matching reference digests never authenticate an independent issuer or permit scoring/production.
